generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, the gap between describing and reflecting is the gap between a log that records what happened in a session and one that asks why a participant responded as they did, or why your own interview manner shaped the data you got. The evaluation stage of self-regulated learning calls this looking back critically, and psychology assessment, from placement logs to lab reports, rewards the reflection that reaches a reason over the account that only reports.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two psychology students write a reflection on the same lab report, which came back with a lower mark than they expected.

Tom writes that the report lost marks on the analysis section and that the feedback said the interpretation went beyond the data. This is accurate, and it is entirely description: it reports what happened and what the feedback said, but it does not ask why the interpretation overreached or what Tom did that led to it. The account stops at what happened.

Amara starts from the same facts, then reflects: the interpretation went beyond the data because she had decided what the study would show before running the analysis, and then read the results to fit. The low mark was not bad luck but a consequence of that expectation. That is a reflection: it reaches a reason, and it points to her own approach.

Both described the same experience accurately. Only Amara reflected on it, by asking why it happened and what her own part was.
generatedProse.summary: Description answers 'what happened'; reflection answers 'so what' and 'why', looking back critically at your own actions and decisions. You can now explain the difference, tell one from the other in a psychology example, and deepen a thin reflection by asking why something happened and what your part in it was. The next lesson takes the understanding you reach and turns it into action.

check.body: In the worked example, what made Amara's account a reflection rather than a description?

items.text: She reached a reason for the low mark and pointed to her own expectation shaping the analysis.
She reported the feedback more accurately than Tom.
She wrote at greater length about the report.
She felt more strongly about the mark.

feedback.correct: That's right. Reaching a reason for the mark, and pointing to her own approach, is what makes it a reflection.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what Amara worked out, beyond reporting the feedback.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara reflected by reaching a reason for the low mark and pointing to her own expectation. Accurate reporting, extra length or a stronger feeling are all still description.
